title: Pressure Control Solenoid "F" Control Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the pressure control solenoid "F" control circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission sets the fluid pressure that applies the clutches during shifts.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Control wire to the pressure control solenoid "F" shorted to voltage or the part open inside
Failed pressure control solenoid "F"
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the pressure control solenoid "F" control circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the pressure control solenoid "F".

title: Transmission Friction Element "G" Apply Time Range/Performance
plain: One of the clutches or bands inside the automatic transmission (element G) is taking longer or shorter than expected to apply during a shift.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Slipping, flare or harsh shifts
Delayed engagement into gear

causes.name: Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Worn clutch pack or band
Sticking pressure control solenoid or valve body
Internal fluid leak from worn seals
Transmission adaptive values need to be reset or relearned

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Look for related solenoid or pressure codes
Have a shop check line pressure and shift data
fix: Start with the fluid and any solenoid faults; worn clutches may need a transmission repair or rebuild.

title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor "B" Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" circuit and has spotted an electrical fault. The transmission computer uses fluid temperature to adjust shift feel and torque converter lock-up.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Shifts may feel firm or delayed
Torque converter may not lock up

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B"
Broken or chafed wire in the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" circuit
Failed transmission fluid temperature sensor "B"
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B".

title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor "B" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" circuit and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. The transmission computer uses fluid temperature to adjust shift feel and torque converter lock-up.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Shifts may feel firm or delayed
Torque converter may not lock up

causes.name: Failing or sticking transmission fluid temperature sensor "B"
Transmission actually running hot or low on fluid
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" circuit reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor "B" Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. The transmission computer uses fluid temperature to adjust shift feel and torque converter lock-up.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Shifts may feel firm or delayed
Torque converter may not lock up

causes.name: Signal wire in the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" circuit shorted to ground or open
Failed transmission fluid temperature sensor "B"
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Unplug the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B" and see if the reading changes
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the transmission fluid temperature sensor "B".

Engine rpm higher than normal at highway speed
Lower fuel economy

title: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off

symptoms: Check engine light on
Shudder or vibration at steady speeds
Engine rpm higher than normal at highway speed
Lower fuel economy

causes.name: Sticking torque converter clutch solenoid
Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Worn torque converter clutch
Worn valve body

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Look for other transmission codes
Have the solenoid tested and commanded with a scan tool
fix: Service the fluid first; if it returns, replace the solenoid, and in some cases the torque converter.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Stuck On
plain: The computer thinks the torque converter clutch pressure control solenoid circuit is stuck on. This solenoid controls the lock-up clutch in the torque converter, which links the engine directly to the transmission at cruising speed.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Shudder or vibration at steady speeds
Engine rpm higher than normal at highway speed
Lower fuel economy
Engine may stall when coming to a stop

causes.name: Sticking torque converter clutch solenoid
Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Worn torque converter clutch
Worn valve body

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Look for other transmission codes
Have the solenoid tested and commanded with a scan tool
fix: Service the fluid first; if it returns, replace the solenoid, and in some cases the torque converter.
drive: Be careful. If the converter stays locked, the engine can stall when you stop, leaving you with heavy steering and harder braking. If it stalls or nearly stalls, don't keep driving; have it towed. If it only shudders, limit driving and get it checked soon.
test_first: Confirm with a scanner whether lockup stays applied at stops, check the solenoid and its wiring for a short, and check the fluid and valve body before replacing the converter.

plain: The computer is watching the 4WD low switch circuit and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. The computer uses this switch to know when four-wheel-drive low range is selected.
symptoms: Check engine or 4WD light on
4WD low may not engage or indicate correctly
Shift timing may be off in 4WD low

causes.name: Failing or sticking 4WD low range switch
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the 4WD low switch circuit reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the 4WD low range switch itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Low Switch Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the 4WD low switch circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. The computer uses this switch to know when four-wheel-drive low range is selected.
symptoms: Check engine or 4WD light on
4WD low may not engage or indicate correctly
Shift timing may be off in 4WD low

causes.name: Signal wire in the 4WD low switch circuit shorted to ground or open
Failed 4WD low range switch
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the 4WD low switch circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the 4WD low range switch.

title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Low Switch Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the 4WD low switch circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. The computer uses this switch to know when four-wheel-drive low range is selected.
symptoms: Check engine or 4WD light on
4WD low may not engage or indicate correctly
Shift timing may be off in 4WD low

causes.name: Signal wire shorted to voltage or a broken ground wire
Failed 4WD low range switch
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the 4WD low switch circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the 4WD low range switch.

title: Upshift Switch Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the upshift switch circuit and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. This switch lets you shift up manually with a paddle or the shift lever.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Manual shift buttons or paddles may not work

causes.name: Worn or sticking switch, sometimes from spilled drinks in the shifter
Failing or sticking upshift switch (paddle or shifter button)
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the upshift switch circuit reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the upshift switch (paddle or shifter button) itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.
